breakfast.name: Jianbing (Crispy Savory Crêpe)
ingredients: Batter: mung bean flour, wheat flour, water
instructions: Spread thin batter on hot round griddle
Crack egg on top, spread with a spatula
Sprinkle scallions and cilantro
Flip when set
Brush with sweet bean paste and chili sauce
Place crispy cracker on top
Fold into thirds
Serve immediately — the contrast of soft crêpe and shatteringly crispy cracker is the whole point
breakfast.description: Beijing's most popular street breakfast — cooked on circular griddles by vendors on every corner. The crunch of the baocui inside the soft egg crêpe is essential.

breakfast.name: Congee (Rice Porridge, 粥)
ingredients: Toppings: preserved egg (pidan), pork floss, scallions, soy sauce, sesame oil, fried dough sticks (youtiao)
instructions: Rinse rice, add to pot with water
Bring to boil, reduce to low simmer
Cook 40-45 min, stirring occasionally — the rice grains break down into silky porridge
The consistency should be flowing, not thick
Ladle into bowls
Top with preserved egg, pork floss, scallions, a drizzle of soy and sesame oil
Serve with youtiao for dipping
breakfast.description: The universal Chinese comfort food — silky rice porridge simmered until the grains dissolve. Every region adds its own toppings.

breakfast.name: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)
ingredients: Dough: 300g flour, hot water, pinch salt
Filling: 300g pork (minced), ginger, scallion, soy sauce, sesame oil, Shaoxing wine, white pepper, sugar
Aspic: rich pork or chicken stock chilled until set, then diced small
instructions: Make dough, rest 30 min
Mix filling with diced aspic — this melts into soup during steaming
Divide dough into small portions, roll very thin wrappers
Pleat 18+ folds around filling, pinch closed at top
Place on parchment in bamboo steamer
Steam 8-10 min
Serve with black vinegar and ginger
To eat: lift carefully by the top knot, place on spoon, bite a small hole, sip the soup, then eat
breakfast.description: Shanghai's legendary soup dumplings — the liquid inside is solidified stock that melts during steaming. The eating technique is a rite of passage.

lunch.name: Kung Pao Chicken (宫保鸡丁)
ingredients: Marinade: soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch
Sauce: 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp black vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp cornstarch, sesame oil
instructions: Marinate chicken 15 min
Mix sauce ingredients in a bowl
Heat wok until smoking, add oil
Fry dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant — do not burn
Add chicken, stir-fry until white
Add garlic, ginger, scallion whites
Pour in sauce, toss until glossy and thick
Add peanuts at the very end — they must stay crunchy
Garnish with scallion greens
lunch.description: Named after a Qing dynasty official — the authentic Sichuan version uses dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorn for málà (numbing-spicy) heat, not sweet sauce.

lunch.name: Mapo Tofu (麻婆豆腐)
instructions: Gently blanch tofu cubes in salted water, drain
Stir-fry pork until crumbly and browned
Push to side, add doubanjiang, fry until oil turns red
Add fermented black beans, garlic, ginger
Add broth, soy sauce, wine
Gently slide in tofu cubes — do not stir roughly or they break
Simmer 5 min, add cornstarch slurry to thicken
Finish with generous ground Sichuan peppercorn and chili oil
lunch.description: Born in a Chengdu restaurant in 1862 — the pockmarked grandmother's tofu. The numbing-spicy-savory combination defines Sichuan cuisine.

lunch.name: Dim Sum: Har Gow & Siu Mai
ingredients: Har gow: wheat starch, tapioca starch, hot water, shrimp, bamboo shoots, sesame oil, white pepper, salt
Siu mai: wonton wrappers, pork, shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch
instructions: Har gow dough: mix wheat starch and tapioca starch with boiling water, knead smooth
Roll thin translucent wrappers
Fill with chopped shrimp and bamboo shoot mixture
Pleat wrapper around filling
Siu mai: mix pork, chopped shrimp, mushroom, season
Fill wonton wrappers, gather around filling leaving top open
Steam both in bamboo steamers 8-10 min
Har gow wrappers should be translucent, revealing the pink shrimp inside
lunch.description: The two pillars of Cantonese dim sum — har gow's translucent shrimp dumplings and siu mai's open-topped pork cups. Yum cha (tea drinking) without them is unthinkable.

lunch.name: Biang Biang Noodles (Hand-Torn Belt Noodles)
ingredients: Dough: 500g high-gluten flour, 250ml water, 1 tsp salt, oil for resting
Chili oil topping: dried chili flakes, Sichuan peppercorn, garlic, sesame oil, neutral oil
instructions: Make dough: mix flour, salt, water. Knead 15 min until very smooth
Rest covered in oil for at least 1 hour (up to 4 hours)
Divide into portions, roll into logs
To pull: hold both ends of a log, slap the middle against the counter repeatedly, stretching
Pull and slap until the noodle is belt-wide — 3-4cm across and very long
Boil noodles 2-3 min (they're thick, so they stay chewy)
Blanch greens in the same water
Top noodles with soy sauce, vinegar, minced garlic, chili flakes
Heat oil until smoking, pour directly over the chili and garlic — the sizzle is the point
Toss and eat — the oil hitting the raw garlic and chili creates the flavor explosion
lunch.description: Xi'an's legendary belt-wide hand-pulled noodles — the slapping technique against the counter and the dramatic sizzle of hot oil over raw chili and garlic are two of the most viral sounds in food content. Named after the most complex Chinese character, which is itself onomatopoeia for the slapping sound.

dinner.name: Peking Duck (北京烤鸭)
ingredients: Hoisin sauce or sweet bean sauce
instructions: Pour boiling water over duck to tighten skin, dry thoroughly
Rub cavity with five-spice and salt
Brush skin with maltose-water mixture
Hang in cool, airy place 12-24 hours until skin is dry as paper (use a fan)
Roast at 240°C for 45-60 min, rotating — skin should be lacquered and shatteringly crispy
Rest 10 min
Carve skin in thin slices (the skin is the star)
Place skin and meat on pancake, add scallion, cucumber, hoisin
Roll and eat
dinner.description: Imperial Beijing's masterpiece — the duck is air-dried for a day, then roasted until the skin is paper-thin and crackling. The skin is served first, and eaten separately for a reason.

dinner.name: Hongshao Rou (Red-Braised Pork Belly, 红烧肉)
instructions: Blanch pork belly cubes, rinse
Caramelize rock sugar in dry wok until amber
Add pork, toss to coat in caramel
Add ginger, star anise, cinnamon, scallions
Add Shaoxing wine, light and dark soy sauce
Add water to just cover
Bring to boil, reduce to gentle simmer
Braise covered 60-75 min until meltingly tender
Uncover, raise heat to reduce sauce until glossy and thick — it should coat each piece
dinner.description: Mao Zedong's favorite dish — Hunan-style red-braised pork belly. The combination of caramelized sugar, soy, and slow braising creates an impossibly rich, glossy sauce.

dinner.name: Sichuan Hot Pot (四川火锅)
ingredients: Broth base: beef tallow, 100g dried chilies, 50g Sichuan peppercorns, doubanjiang, garlic, ginger, star anise, cassia bark, fennel, cloves, white cardamom
Dipping ingredients: thinly sliced beef, lamb, tofu, mushrooms, leafy greens, glass noodles, lotus root, quail eggs
Dipping sauce: sesame oil, minced garlic, oyster sauce, cilantro
instructions: Melt beef tallow, fry dried chilies and peppercorns until fragrant
Add doubanjiang, fry until oil turns deep red
Add aromatics and spices
Add stock, bring to rolling boil
Transfer to tabletop burner
Each person cooks ingredients in the bubbling broth — thin meat takes 10 seconds, vegetables a bit longer
Dip into sesame oil-garlic sauce before eating
Keep adding ingredients and broth as you go
dinner.description: Chengdu's communal feast — a bubbling cauldron of chili oil, Sichuan peppercorn, and dozens of ingredients cooked tableside. The numbing heat builds over the meal.

snacks.name: Scallion Pancakes (葱油饼)
instructions: Mix flour with boiling water and cold water to form soft dough, rest 20 min
Roll flat, brush with sesame oil and salt
Scatter scallions generously
Roll into a log, coil into a spiral, flatten into disc
Fry in oil until golden and flaky on both sides
Cut into wedges
snacks.description: Shatteringly flaky layered pancakes with scallion — the coiling technique creates dozens of thin layers that separate into crispy sheets.

snacks.name: Baozi (Steamed Buns)
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 250ml warm water, 7g yeast, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp oil
Filling: 400g ground pork, cabbage (chopped, salted, squeezed), ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper
instructions: Mix dough, knead until smooth, rise 1 hour
Mix filling ingredients
Divide dough into rounds, roll wrappers thick in center, thin at edges
Fill, pleat closed at top
Rise 15 min
Steam 12-15 min — the buns should be white and puffy
Do not open the steamer lid immediately — wait 2 min or they collapse
snacks.description: Fluffy steamed buns stuffed with juicy pork and cabbage — breakfast, lunch, or snack, they're everywhere in China.

snacks.name: Jianbing (Street Crepe)
ingredients: Batter: mung bean flour, wheat flour, water
instructions: Spread batter in thin circle on large round griddle
Crack egg directly onto crepe, spread with scraper
Sprinkle sesame seeds and green onion
Flip the crepe
Brush with hoisin and chili sauce
Place crispy cracker in center
Add pickled vegetables and cilantro
Fold the edges over into a rectangular packet
Cut in half and hand to customer
The entire process takes under 90 seconds — the speed is part of the show
snacks.description: China's most famous breakfast street food — a savory crepe made on a giant round griddle in under 90 seconds. The egg-crack-and-spread, the cracker insertion, and the fold-and-cut are choreography. Jianbing-making videos are permanently viral — it's the world's most-watched street food being made.

desserts.name: Tangyuan (Glutinous Rice Balls)
ingredients: Filling: black sesame paste, sugar, lard (or peanut butter)
Ginger syrup: ginger, water, rock sugar
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with water to smooth dough
Make filling: grind black sesame with sugar and lard into paste
Wrap small balls of filling inside rice dough balls
Make ginger syrup: simmer ginger with rock sugar
Boil tangyuan until they float, then 2 more min
Serve in warm ginger syrup
desserts.description: Sweet rice balls filled with molten black sesame — served during Lantern Festival and Winter Solstice. The round shape symbolizes family togetherness.

desserts.name: Egg Tarts (蛋挞)
ingredients: Pastry: 200g flour, 100g butter, 50g powdered sugar, 1 egg yolk, water
Custard: 3 eggs, 150ml milk, 100ml cream, 80g sugar, vanilla
instructions: Make pastry, chill, press into tart molds
Whisk custard ingredients, strain for smoothness
Fill tart shells three-quarters full
Bake at 210°C for 20-25 min until custard is just set with charred spots on top
Cool slightly — the custard jiggles when done right
desserts.description: Cantonese-Portuguese egg tarts — silky custard in flaky pastry. A dim sum trolley staple and the pride of Macau.

drinks.name: Bubble Tea (珍珠奶茶)
instructions: Cook tapioca pearls according to package — usually 20 min boiling, then soak in sugar syrup
Brew strong black tea, cool
Mix tea with milk and sugar syrup to taste
Add ice
Spoon tapioca pearls into glass
Pour tea over
Serve with wide straw
drinks.description: Invented in Taiwan in the 1980s — now a global phenomenon. The chewy tapioca pearls (boba) at the bottom are the whole reason for the fat straw.

drinks.name: Chinese Tea (Gongfu Ceremony)
ingredients: High-quality loose tea (oolong, pu-erh, or green)
instructions: Warm gaiwan and cups with hot water
Add tea leaves — fill gaiwan one-third full
First infusion: pour water over leaves, discard after 10 seconds (this washes and opens the leaves)
Second infusion: steep 20-30 seconds, pour into cups
Each subsequent steep adds 5-10 seconds
The same leaves yield 8-15 infusions, each with evolving flavor
drinks.description: Not a recipe but a practice — gongfu tea ceremony is the Chinese art of tea. Short steeps from the same leaves, each cup slightly different. The vessel matters as much as the leaf.
